children: into the U.S. litigation escrow account, a move that results in the dilution of its B-1, B-2, and B-3 common stock, which is predominantly held by U.S. financial institutions and their affiliates. The account, funded by proceeds from Visa's IPO, covers certain litigation obligations.
The change in the conversion rate has the same effect on earnings per share as buying back its class A common stock.

Under the terms of the company's U.S. retrospective responsibility plan, when the company funds the U.S. litigation account, the conversion rates of the class B-1, class B-2, and class B-3 shares to class A common stock are reduced.

This latest deposit reduced the conversion rate for class B-1 common stock to 1.5400 class A shares from 1.5445. The rate for B-2 shares dropped to 1.4924 class A shares from 1.5014. The conversion rate for class B-3 shares fell to 1.4773 from 1.4953, effective as of Sept. 18, 2026.
stock edged up 0.1% in after-hours trading.
